semantics.clock: All sequential state updates on positive edge of clk
semantics.sampling: Every positive edge samples all eight input bits
semantics.equation: After positive edge n, anyedge[i] equals 1 iff input sample n differs from input sample n-1 at bit i, for n >= 2
semantics.latency: Registered detection at the next positive edge after an inter-edge input transition; output held until next positive edge
semantics.reset: No reset port or reset behavior specified
semantics.initialization: No initialization imposed; first output sample unspecified because no previous sample exists
semantics.independence: Each output bit detects both rising and falling sampled transitions independently; input changes that return before sampling are not detected

numeric.type: Eight independent unsigned one-bit Boolean signals
numeric.operation: Bitwise change detection; no arithmetic, rounding, saturation or overflow
numeric.width: Input history and output each exactly eight bits
numeric.unknowns: Four-state unknown inputs are outside specified binary behavior; no special unknown filtering

verification.oracle: Independent per-bit comparison of current and preceding sampled input, using inequality rather than vector XOR
verification.startup: Skip first output assertion, then check every sampled result
verification.directed: Stable zero and one, each bit rising and falling, simultaneous changes, alternating vectors, consecutive transitions
verification.exhaustive: Check every pair of eight-bit previous and current input vectors
verification.between_edges: Assert output holds when input changes between positive edges, including a pulse returning before sampling
verification.tools: Icarus v12, -g2012, explicit dev_tb top, finite timeout on compile and simulation
verification.acceptance: Self-checking simulation terminates with PASS and no mismatches; contract gate is structural only

specification_ambiguities: Power-up and first-cycle values are unspecified; no initial value or reset is added.
Cycle-after-transition is interpreted as registered comparison of consecutive positive-edge samples.
